paragraphs: The A7L is the suit that walked on the Moon. It was sewn rather than machined, by seamstresses working to tolerances measured in fractions of an inch, and every layer of it had one job: keep a person alive in vacuum while still allowing them to bend down and pick up a rock.
The suit holds 25,669 polygons and 26,379 vertices in quads and tris with mixed UV layout, and comes rigged so it can be posed or animated. It is built to CheckMate specification.
At $149 it suits space history and documentary work, museum and exhibition material, education, film and television, game characters and editorial illustration. On sale since 2026.
Healthcare scenes fail without staff in them. An empty ward reads as closed, and a patient alone reads as neglected, so the nurse is the figure that turns a modelled interior into a working hospital.

The character is deliberately light at 11,719 polygons and 12,575 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, suited to crowds and background use, and comes rigged for posing or animation. It is built to CheckMate specification.

At $149 it suits healthcare and hospital visualisation, medical education and patient material, architectural interiors, advertising, film previsualisation and editorial illustration. On sale since 2025.

A pit garage is a workshop that has to be packed into a shipping crate between races. Everything is on wheels, everything is modular, and the layout is identical from circuit to circuit because a crew that has to think about where a tool is has already lost time.

The scene holds 189,788 polygons and 193,980 vertices in quads and tris with overlapping UVs, suited to the repeated panelling and equipment, and comes rigged so parts of it can be posed or animated. It is built to CheckMate specification.
At $149 it suits motorsport visualisation and broadcast graphics, automotive advertising, film and television, game environments and editorial illustration. On sale since 2025.

The Dauphin is quiet for its size, which is exactly why police forces bought it. A shrouded tail rotor cuts the noise that gives a helicopter away, and an aircraft that can loiter over a city without announcing itself is worth more than a faster one.

The airframe holds 250,368 polygons and 260,239 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, textured with 42 maps all at 4096x4096. It carries CheckMate Lite and Pro certification, and a rigged build is offered separately.
At $149 it suits law enforcement and public safety visualisation, film and television, flight simulation, game environments and editorial illustration. On sale since 2017.

Reconnaissance aircraft are built around their sensors and painted to disappear. Grey is not a livery choice, it is the whole point: an aeroplane whose job is to see without being seen has no reason to carry a single mark that would help anyone identify it.

The airframe holds 187,404 polygons and 102,834 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, and comes rigged for posing or animation. Native rigged builds for Cinema 4D and Maya are offered separately, and it carries CheckMate Lite and Pro certification.
At $149 it suits defence and aviation visualisation, flight simulation, documentary and news graphics, game environments and editorial illustration. On sale since 2023.

A greeting pose is a small thing that changes the whole tone of a render. A road worker raising a hand turns a construction scene from an obstacle into people at work, which is usually what a client actually wants the image to say.

The figure is very light at 8,563 polygons and 9,228 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, built for background and crowd use, and textured with 19 maps, 14 at 4096x4096, 2 at 3000x3000 and 3 at 1000x1000. It carries StemCell certification.
At $149 it suits infrastructure and construction visualisation, safety and training material, architectural and urban scenes, advertising and editorial illustration. On sale since 2020.

The MC-21 was Russia's attempt to build a narrow body that could compete on its own terms, and its most interesting feature is the wing: composite, and made domestically after export restrictions cut off the original supplier. The programme became a test of whether that was possible at all.

The airframe holds 146,741 polygons and 160,461 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, textured with 12 maps, 5 at 8192x8192, 4 at 4096x4096 and 3 at 2048x2048. It carries CheckMate Lite and Pro certification, and a rigged build is offered separately.
At $149 it suits aviation visualisation, flight simulation, news and documentary graphics, film backgrounds and editorial illustration. On sale since 2018.

The Orlan is a suit you climb into through a hatch in the back, which is why a cosmonaut can put one on alone in minutes while an American suit needs help and an hour. That single design decision shapes the whole silhouette: rigid torso, soft limbs, a door where the backpack should be.

The figure holds 75,244 polygons and 79,060 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, textured with 21 maps, 20 at 4096x4096 and one at 512x512. It carries CheckMate Lite and Pro certification, and a rigged build is offered separately.
At $149 it suits space programme visualisation, documentary and news graphics, museum and education work, film, game characters and editorial illustration. On sale since 2015.

A fast jet pilot wears a system rather than clothing: a pressure garment that squeezes the legs under load, a helmet that carries the oxygen mask and the comms, and a harness that ties all of it to the seat. Sand coloured means desert operations, and nothing else.
The figure holds 70,649 polygons and 74,014 vertices in quads and tris with mixed UV layout, and comes rigged so it can be posed in a cockpit or standing. It is built to CheckMate specification.
At $149 it suits defence and aviation visualisation, flight simulation, documentary and film, game characters and editorial illustration. On sale since 2026.

The Skycrane has no fuselage worth speaking of, and that is deliberate. It is a spine, an engine and a lifting hook, so whatever it carries hangs where a cabin would otherwise be. Fitted with a tank, it becomes the aircraft that refills from a lake in under a minute and goes back to the fire.

The airframe holds 565,022 polygons and 609,970 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, textured with 31 maps all at 4096x4096. It carries CheckMate Lite and Pro certification, and a rigged build is offered separately.
At $149 it suits emergency services and wildfire visualisation, documentary and news graphics, film and television, flight simulation and game environments. On sale since 2020.

Airship hangars are among the largest enclosed spaces ever built, and they had to be: the thing inside cannot be tilted, folded or taken apart. Several still stand long after the airships left, used as film stages and warehouses because nothing else that big exists.

The scene holds 191,989 polygons and 225,473 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, supplying the hangar together with the blimp inside. It carries CheckMate Lite and Pro certification, and a rigged build is offered separately.
At $139 it suits aviation history and documentary work, museum and exhibition material, architectural and industrial scenes, film backgrounds and game environments. On sale since 2022.

Body on frame is the older way to build a car: a ladder chassis carrying the running gear, and a body dropped on top of it. It survives in trucks and off roaders because the frame takes the punishment, and stripping the two apart is the clearest way to explain how a vehicle is actually assembled.
The model holds 153,700 polygons and 153,393 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, showing the body together with its frame. It is built to CheckMate specification.
At $139 it suits automotive engineering visualisation, technical and training material, manufacturing presentation, education, film and game environments. On sale since 2024.

The driver's seat is the one component of a car that every occupant touches and judges. Bolstering, headrest shape, stitching and the angle of the base all change how a cabin reads, which is why a collection is more useful than any single seat.
This is a collection listing rather than a single object, supplied as static pieces. It carries CheckMate Lite and Pro certification, and two further volumes of the set are offered separately.
At $139 the set suits automotive interior visualisation, configurators and marketing, furniture and product presentation, game environments and editorial illustration. On sale since 2024.

Put one figure in a construction render and the whole image acquires scale. The hardhat and high visibility vest are legible at any distance and in any resolution, which is why this silhouette does more for a site visualisation than any amount of added detail elsewhere.

The figure holds 48,147 polygons and 49,309 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, textured with 25 maps, 18 at 4096x4096, 6 at 2048x2048 and one at 512x512. It carries CheckMate Lite and Pro certification and is supplied in a standing pose.
At $139 it suits construction and architectural visualisation, safety and training material, equipment marketing, infrastructure presentation and editorial illustration. On sale since 2017.
